descripcion: At B1 you learn the most common everyday phrasal verbs: get up, look for, find out. These are used constantly in spoken English, and avoiding them in favour of more formal one-word verbs makes ordinary speech sound stiff and unnatural.

ejemplos.texto: I usually get up at seven in the morning.
I'm looking for a new apartment.
I found out yesterday that the shop is closed.

notas: Get up, look for and find out are among the most frequent phrasal verbs in everyday English.
Look for takes an object directly: I'm looking for my keys.
Find out can be followed by a whole clause: I found out that she moved.

contraste.es: Spanish has no phrasal verbs, so the first word that comes to mind is often a Latin-based verb (discover instead of find out). These verbs exist in English but sound more formal.
contraste.de: German separable verbs are a close model (herausfinden – find out, aufstehen – get up), so everyday phrasal verbs feel natural to German speakers.
contraste.it: Italian verbs with a particle (andare via – go away, tirare fuori – take out) are a good model, so everyday phrasal verbs are easy to understand.
contraste.fr: French has no phrasal verbs, so the first word that comes to mind is often a Latin-based verb (découvrir – discover instead of find out), which sounds more formal in English.
contraste.pt: Portuguese has no phrasal verbs, so the first word that comes to mind is often a Latin-based verb (descobrir – discover instead of find out), which sounds more formal in English.

errores: Using a formal one-word verb (discover) instead of the everyday phrasal verb (find out).
Forgetting the preposition in look for.
Splitting a phrasal verb that shouldn't be split.
autochequeo: Have I used at least four different phrasal verbs?
Is the preposition correct for each one?
Have I avoided a formal one-word verb where a phrasal verb fits better?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on everyday phrasal verbs. Check the preposition used in each one and suggest a phrasal verb wherever a formal one-word verb was used instead. Do not rewrite the text.

es: *recoger a alguien* rendered as *recollect someone* instead of *pick someone up*.
de: *abnehmen* rendered as *take off*: *I took off five kilos* instead of *I lost five kilos*.
it: *andare a prendere* rendered as *go to take someone* instead of *pick someone up*.
fr: *aller chercher quelqu'un* rendered as *go search someone* instead of *pick someone up*.
pt: *ir buscar alguém* rendered as *go search someone* instead of *pick someone up*.
